newsitem.title: USA: MGM licenses films, TV shows to KirchGroup.
newsitem.headline: MGM licenses films, TV shows to KirchGroup.

text.p: Film studio Metro Goldwyn Mayer Inc on Monday said it will license films and television programming to German pay-television provider KirchGroup.
Financial terms were undisclosed, but an MGM spokeswoman said it was valued "in the hundreds of millions" of dollars.

Under the deal, KirchGroup's Taurus Films will have non-exclusive rights to broadcast MGM films and television shows on its digital television network, DF1, until mid-1998. At that time, it will acquire rights to MGM's current films, television movies and some of its library for five years. MGM holds an option to extend the deal for another five years.
A separate agreement was made for MGM's James Bond catalog of films including the upcoming, "Tomorrow Never Dies."
"We are delighted with this deal which marks the most significant international pay television agreement ever for MGM," Gary Marenzi, president of MGM Telecommunications Group, said in a statement.
MGM's library includes more than 1500 feature films and 2,600 hours of television programming. It also controls a 4,500-title home video library.
Earlier today, MGM announced an agreement to acquire a 2,200-film library and other entertainment assets from Metromedia International Group Inc.
KirchGroup owns interests in two commercial channels in Germany, SAT 1 and sports channel DSF. It also owns satellite broadcaster DF1, as well as other distribution assets.
